land.text: the First and Second Republics of 1810-1814

predecessors.note: Same name and Q717 (the page's infobox 'Declared: 5 July 1811'); the royalist reconquest and Gran Colombia lie between, so the republic-of-venezuela dossier is kept separate and listed here only as the earlier republic.

capitals.name: Caracas
capitals.note: 'The capital and largest urban agglomeration is Caracas.'

correction.text: Venezuela on its modern outline after the separation from Gran Colombia (1830)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's row begins in 1834 but the page has Venezuela independent of Gran Colombia in 1830 (infobox 13 January 1830; body 22 September). Cliopatria keeps Venezuela inside Gran Colombia's 1830-1833 shape (marked wrong in the gran-colombia dossier).

934,696 km2 for 1834-1852 against the infobox 916,445 km2 (body 912,050 km2; undated; ratio 1.02): modern Venezuela (3,853 of its 3,894 cells) plus 55 border cells of Colombia, Brazil and Guyana. The Guayana Esequiba (159,500 km2 west of the Essequibo, claimed by Venezuela) is not drawn: Britain commissioned the Schomburgk survey in 1840 (the page also says 1835) and 'declared the Schomburgk Line the provisional frontier of British Guiana' in October 1886. The Colombian and Brazilian lines are drawn as the modern ones (1859 treaty with Brazil, 1891 award and 1941 treaty with Colombia).
935,099 km2 for 1853-1876: the 1834 outline plus one Amazonas border cell (about 250 km2), rasterisation noise; no event on the page.

933,752 km2 for 1877-1899: eleven cells differ from 1853 (7 lost in eastern Bolívar, the Delta Amacuro edge and Guyana's Pomeroon-Supenaam; 4 gained along the Brazilian border and in Bolívar). The Guayana Esequiba page dates Britain's provisional frontier to October 1886 and the arbitration to 1899, not 1877, and the Brazil border page gives no 1877 event (unverified: the date and the cells stand as Cliopatria's, confidence 1 in the ledger).

937,211 km2 for 1900-1986: the 1899 Paris award reflected: Venezuela 'received Barima Point ... giving it undisputed control of the river' and the border at the Wenamu River, while Britain 'received most of the disputed territory and all of the gold mines'; the shape adds 8 cells of Delta Amacuro. The mixed commission began demarcating in 1900 and 'signed off on the border in 1905'. The Essequibo is not drawn; Venezuela denounced the award on 12 November 1962 and signed the Geneva Agreement on 17 February 1966. Ankoko Island is occupied from October 1966 (ledger).

The same outline for 1987-2023 (937,211 km2). The ICJ accepted Guyana's case on 18 December 2020 and the Venezuelan referendum of 3 December 2023 took no vote in the disputed region; no change of border is drawn.

ledger.note: 1830: Venezuela becomes a separate state. The page gives 'from Gran Colombia: 13 January 1830' (infobox) and 'allowed the proclamation of a newly independent Venezuela, on 22 September' (body); the state was the 'Estado de Venezuela' (1830-1856). The gran-colombia dossier has the Valencia congress of 6 May 1830.
1856: the State of Venezuela becomes the Republic. 'Estado de Venezuela (1830-1856), República de Venezuela (1856-1864)'; the page gives no month.
1864: the United States of Venezuela, after the Federal War (1859-63). 'Estados Unidos de Venezuela (1864-1953)'; the page gives no month.

region.text: the cells of eastern Bolívar and the Orinoco delta edge that the 1853 outline has and the 1877-1899 outline lacks (7 cells), on the side of the Schomburgk Line

ledger.note: 1877: Cliopatria's outline shrinks by seven cells on the British Guiana side (about 1,800 km2). The page dates the Schomburgk Line to a survey 'commissioned in 1840' and its provisional adoption to 'October 1886', and is silent on 1877, so the date is Cliopatria's and the reading as a loss to British Guiana is the researcher's.

region.text: four border cells added in 1877: two in Roraima, one in Amazonas and one in Bolívar

ledger.note: 1877: four cells are added on the Brazilian side. The Brazil-Venezuela border page says the border was 'delimited by the Treaty of Limits and River Navigation of May 5, 1859' and 'ratified by the Protocol of 1929'; it mentions no 1877 event and no territory exchanged, so this is a bridging entry for Cliopatria's change (page silent).

region.text: Barima Point and the mouth of the Orinoco ('giving it undisputed control of the river') and the border at the Wenamu River: the land of the 1900 outline that the 1877-1899 outline lacks (about 14 cells, mostly Delta Amacuro)

ledger.note: 1899: the Paris Award gives Venezuela the Orinoco mouth. 'On 3 October 1899 the Tribunal' ruled largely for Britain, but Venezuela 'received Barima Point ... giving it undisputed control of the river' and the border at the Wenamu River; the mixed commission began demarcating in 1900. Cliopatria draws it from 1900.
1953: back to the Republic. 'República de Venezuela (1953-1999)'; the page gives no month.

region.text: Ankoko Island, 'at the confluence of the Cuyuni River and Wenamu River' (6°43′N 61°8′W)

ledger.note: 1966: Venezuelan troops occupy Ankoko Island. 'Venezuelan troops began their occupation of Ankoko Island in October 1966', soon building 'military installations and an airstrip'; 'Guyana says Venezuela occupies the Guyanese side of the island'. The page reports no end: the island is still under Venezuelan administration.
1999: the Bolivarian Republic of Venezuela, 'the full official title since the adoption of the Constitution of 1999' (20 December 1999).

wars.name: Federal War
wars.outcome: A civil war without territorial change; 'This culminated in the Federal War (1859-63)' and the state became the United States of Venezuela in 1864.
wars.note: The Treaty of Coche is not on the page.

wars.name: Venezuela crisis of 1895

zones.text: Barima Point and the mouth of the Orinoco ('giving it undisputed control of the river') and the border at the Wenamu River: the land of the 1900 outline that the 1877-1899 outline lacks (about 14 cells, mostly Delta Amacuro)

wars.outcome: The Paris Arbitral Award of 3 October 1899 gave Britain most of the disputed territory and all of the gold mines, and Venezuela Barima Point and the river's mouth; demarcation 1900-1905.
wars.note: 'The dispute became a diplomatic crisis in 1895, when Venezuela hired William Lindsay Scruggs as its lobbyist in Washington'; the US under Cleveland took up Venezuela's Monroe Doctrine argument. No ground was fought for; the zone is the land that changed hands in the award.

wars.name: Venezuela crisis of 1902-1903
wars.outcome: Britain, Germany and Italy 'imposed a naval blockade'; no change of border.
wars.note: The page gives no month and no settlement.

wars.name: Guayana Esequiba dispute

zones.text: Ankoko Island, 'at the confluence of the Cuyuni River and Wenamu River' (6°43′N 61°8′W)

wars.outcome: Unsettled: Venezuela denounced the 1899 award before the United Nations in 1945 and 'formally raised the issue again' there in 1962, the Geneva Agreement was signed on 17 February 1966, Venezuelan troops occupied Ankoko Island in October 1966, the ICJ accepted the case on 18 December 2020 and Venezuela's referendum of 3 December 2023 claimed the area.
wars.note: The claim covers 159,500 km2 west of the Essequibo River; only Ankoko Island is held by Venezuela, so the claimed area is not a zone.

certainty.note: The British Guiana frontier was disputed (Schomburgk Line 1840-1886, award 1899); the Brazilian line was a treaty from 5 May 1859 but undemarcated, and the Colombian line rested on the 1891 award; the pages give no surveys.

The British Guiana frontier follows the 1899 award demarcated 1900-1905, the Brazilian line the 1859 treaty ratified by the 1929 protocol, the Colombian line the 1891 award and the 1941 treaty. The exceptions are soft: the Guayana Esequiba claim (159,500 km2), Ankoko Island and the Gulf of Venezuela.

notes: ONE STATE OR TWO. Cliopatria's 'Republic of Venezuela' (1811-1814) and 'Venezuela' (1834-2024) share Q717 but are different states in this project: the republic-of-venezuela dossier (another part) keeps the First and Second Republics apart; this dossier lists it and gran-colombia as predecessors and starts in 1830. Cliopatria's six shapes are the modern outline (3,905-3,916 cells); only 1877 and 1900 change by a few cells. Not settled: (1) the 1877 shift (7 cells lost, 4 gained) is on no page opened; its two ledger entries are confidence 1. (2) The 13 January vs 22 September 1830 dates are the page's own conflict; the gran-colombia dossier has 6 May. (3) The Guayana Esequiba (159,500 km2) is claimed, not held, and is not drawn; the Venezuelan side's contest zone was left out because no ground was fought for. (4) Ankoko Island is a single cell: the occupation has no end because the page reports none, so the validator warns about the unpaired start. (5) The Brazil page names a 1904 Pirara arbitration (Brazil-Britain) and says Brazil does not recognise Venezuela's claim; it gives no territory exchanged with Venezuela. (6) The Colombian frontier (Gulf of Venezuela, Los Monjes) and the 1833-34 treaty are not on the pages. Page budget: five pages of five.
